sub: The deal didn't die on price. It died in the 11 days before anyone followed up.
caption:
Most "sales problems" are actually memory problems.

The deal didn't die because the pitch was weak. It died in the 11 days between "send me a proposal" and someone remembering to follow up.

Pull your last 20 lost deals. Tag each: never qualified, lost on merit, or went dark after a specific step.

Most teams expect mostly "lost on merit." They find mostly "went dark."

You don't have a talent gap. You have one unowned handoff leaking pipeline, invisibly, every month.

Name the handoff. Name the owner. Set the clock.

sub: An AI agent calling tools, or an expense booked at a branch nobody's watching. Same rule.
caption:
An automation you can't audit isn't an asset. It's a liability you haven't been billed for yet.

The difference shows up at the worst moment: an auditor asks, a customer disputes a charge, a regulator wants the trail.

For any process that touches money or data, can you answer in under five minutes, without asking a person: who did it, when, what changed, who approved it, and has anything been edited since?

If the answer is "we'd have to check a few places," it's running on trust, not evidence.

Trust is fine. Until the day it isn't.

headline.t: It's left in plain text — in a config file.

sub: Keep secrets out of code. Rotate anything exposed. Scan before you ship.

footer.text: One of MCP Shield's 5 checks looks for exactly this:

caption:
A common way to leak a password is to write it down where it works perfectly: inside a config file.

It feels harmless. The app needs the key, you paste it into settings, you ship. Nothing breaks.

Then that file lands in a Git repo, a backup, a screenshot, or a tool description an AI agent reads automatically. Now your live credential is in places you never meant it to be.

The fix is boring and it works:
— Keep secrets out of code (env vars / a secrets manager).
— Rotate any key you suspect is exposed. Assume exposed means compromised.
— Scan before things ship, not after.

→ aegibit.com/products/mcp-shield
